mechanism.base: Wood is what a fire is made of before it is a fire. The warmth sits in the grain of a dry branch for years, waiting on one spark, and once the branch takes the flame has its shape and its hours. Fed on green wood a fire smokes and sulks, and fed on seasoned wood it burns steady into the night and leaves embers hot enough to start the morning.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Wood, the fire has nothing long to feed on, a bright start that drops to embers before the work is done. Keep one slow book going beside the fast ones.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Wood, the logs are stacked higher than the flame can climb, so much to take in that nothing gets lit. Finish one small thing before you read another word.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Wood makes it grow. As a catalyst, the intake falls behind the output, and you would rather puzzle an answer out alone than take one from a teacher. Either way you run dry before you feel taught.
function.definition_friction: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Growing is what Wood makes of it. As a friction, intake outruns use and you take in more than you decide, your odd way or the way home taught you. You keep what you know where nobody learns it.
function.advise_catalyst: You give out faster than you take in, and running on your own fuel feels like energy until it runs out. Take a class in something nobody pays you for. Keep one evening a week with no plans. Ask someone older how they did it and listen past the first sentence. Nap before the next idea.
function.advise_friction: Seek Metal, the Action energy. Metal is the finished line: it decides, it ships, it dates the thing you keep studying. Let it spend what Wood piles up. You keep learning past the point of use because being judged feels worse than being unready. Decide one open question by a written date. Hand someone one unfinished page.

candidates.cta_verdict: You learn by growing an idea rather than collecting it, so you understand late and keep it for good.

catalyst.clause: The fire has nothing long to feed on, a bright start that drops to embers.
catalyst.remedy: Keep one slow book going beside the fast ones.

friction.clause: The logs are stacked higher than the flame can climb.
friction.remedy: Finish one small thing before you read another word.

wide.clause: Wood is one thing you never run short of, the fuel laid ready for your fire.
wide.remedy: Light something with it this week.

missing.clause: Nothing dry to put on the fire, so it lives on quick scraps and goes out early.
missing.remedy: Ask someone older for the long version once a week.

spared.clause: No Wood to pile on, and the fire is brighter for the open air.
spared.remedy: Act on what you already know.

thin.clause: A little Wood in the fire, enough to catch and not enough to smother it.
thin.remedy: Keep it small. One book at a time.

excess.clause: Wood piled past use and the fire blazes past its task, all flare and no lasting warmth.
excess.remedy: Take in less. Put one idea to work.

mechanism_yin.base: Wood is warm by nature and fire sleeps inside it, the classics say, so every flame is fed by what was gathered before it: dry branches, stacked seasons, years of quiet growth surrendered to one bright hour. A flame is only ever as tall as its fuel. The small light borrows everything from what was gathered.

retired_2026-09-20_evaluation_rulings.mechanism.friction_turn: Run heavy, the woodpile buries the fire: fuel hoarded past burning, preparation stacked so high the flame never gets lit. Pull a branch off the pile and strike.

carry.friction.clause: The woodpile buries the fire: fuel hoarded past burning, preparation stacked so high the flame never gets lit.
carry.friction.remedy: Pull a branch off the pile and strike.

carry.excess.clause: Too much wood chokes the fire: fuel stacked past burning, the flame smothered by its own supply.

carry.spared.clause: Wood runs absent, and the fire is not smothered: nothing hoarded, nothing postponed.
carry.spared.remedy: Keep it. Gather only what you will burn.

__ore.retired_fn_body: The Root is your learning function: the seat where the world soaks in and becomes yours. With Wood running it, your mind absorbs like a canopy: reaching for new material, grafting idea onto idea until strange hybrids fruit. You learn by gathering and by growing, and every book, mentor, and friendship becomes future firelight. Keep planting. Your brilliance burns what your curiosity stacked.
__ore.retired_base_personal: Your core is Fire, and Wood feeds Fire: dry branches make the flame. Everything gathered and grown, books read, friendships tended, skills stacked like cordwood, is the fuel your light actually burns. That is why Wood is your Mind, the intake that restores what shining spends. A fire is not kept alive by burning harder. It is kept alive by the woodpile.

backlog_dips_tg_pattern.body: Green time restores the thinker: gardens, walks, and living things refill your fuel.

__ore.retired_v3_definition_catalyst:
Wood is your Mind, and as a catalyst, it is how your fuel accumulates: skills stacked, books finished, friendships tended, people learned from over years. What you gather quietly becomes what you later spend as brilliance.

Curious, collecting, in it for the long arc. The bookshelf is a biography, the mentors are chosen carefully, and the flash of insight that impresses everyone was in fact ten quiet years arriving on time.

Brilliance is mostly patience with good storage. Keep one slow project that grows monthly, a course, a craft, a language, and refuse to rush it. Finish books. Choose one person to learn from properly this year and stay teachable.
__ore.retired_v3_definition_friction:
Wood is your Mind, and as a friction, it is gathering as a way of postponing: one more certification, one more plan, readiness that keeps moving its own finish line.

Prepared, credentialed, still waiting. The folder of plans is immaculate, the qualifications outnumber the attempts, and every new course quietly buys another season of not being tested. Somewhere the learning stopped being fuel and became shelter.

Readiness is proven only in the open. Book the thing you have been training for, this month, at whatever level you are. Let one plan ship at eighty percent. When the urge to prepare rises, ask what it is protecting you from.
